name: A Passive Coordinate Determines Two Nested Ample Shores
statement: In the active/passive normalization of an ample pair $K\subsetneq A$, fix a passive coordinate $z$ and put $M_z=\{u\in Q_Y:\widehat u^{\oplus z}\in K\}$. Then $S_z=D\cap M_z$. Whenever nonempty, each of $L\cap M_z$, $B\cap M_z$, $L\cup M_z$, and $B\cup M_z$ is ample. Moreover $(B\cap M_z)\setminus(L\cap M_z)=S_z$ and $(B\cup M_z)\setminus(L\cup M_z)=D\setminus S_z$. Thus a passive boundary type and its complement are relative facets of two nested ample pairs on the same active coordinates.
proof: Condition $K$ on the common passive assignment outside $z$. Its two sections are $L$ and $M_z$; the two-layer shadow-intersection lemma makes their union and intersection ample. The same conditioning of $A$ has sections $B$ and $M_z$, because every relative concept lies on the common passive side, so the same lemma handles the two families involving $B$. The shore identities follow from $B=L\mathbin{\dot\cup}D$ and the definition of $M_z$.
